1.title: Vision and Image Generation Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Vision and Image Generation Applications. It covers the exam area Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model. Create new visual outputs by using generative models. Build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Three vision tasks
1.text: Three vision tasks. Interpret an image. Direction: Image in, text out. What you use: A multimodal model (vision-enabled) with the image in the prompt. Create an image. Direction: Text in, image out. What you use: An image-generation model. Analyze an image with a ready-made service. Direction: Image in, structured result out. What you use: Azure Vision image analysis (captions, tags, objects, Read).

1.title: Three vision tasks, continued
1.text: Three vision tasks. The figure shows this: Three vision tasks: interpret with a multimodal model, create with an image model, analyze with Azure Vision.

1.title: Interpret visual input in a prompt
1.text: Interpret visual input in a prompt. A vision-enabled multimodal model accepts an image together with text in the same prompt, so you can ask about the picture: "Describe this picture", "What is wrong with this product?", "How many tents are in the photo?". Vision-enabled models include the G P T five series, G P T four point one series, G P T four oh series and the O series reasoning models. The message content is a list of parts: a text part and an image part. The image is given as a U R L or as base sixty-four-encoded data.

1.title: Interpret visual input in a prompt, continued
1.text: Interpret visual input in a prompt. Image limits exist (size and format, for example about twenty megabytes and common formats such as J P E G and P N G). This is the shape of a request from the Microsoft documentation (the older chat completions style). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Interpret visual input in a prompt, continued
1.text: Interpret visual input in a prompt. model deployment name. The deployment of a vision-enabled model. role system. The assistant's rules (Module six). role user with a list. The prompt has several parts. type text,... The question about the image. type image url,... The image, by U R L (or base sixty-four data). max tokens. The maximum length of the reply. Exam tip: "The prompt includes an image" to the user message content is a list with a text part and an image part. The model must be vision-enabled. A text-only model rejects or ignores images.

1.title: Create new images with generative models
1.text: Create new images with generative models. An image-generation model creates an image from a text prompt. You choose the deployment, the prompt, the number of images, the size and the quality. For gpt image-one, sizes include one thousand twenty-four times one thousand twenty-four, one thousand twenty-four times one thousand five hundred thirty-six and one thousand five hundred thirty-six times one thousand twenty-four; quality can be low, medium or high. The result comes back as base sixty-four image data (no U R L), which your app decodes and saves or shows. Model names change quickly: dall e-three was retired on March four, two thousand twenty-six; current G P T-Image models are used instead.

1.title: Create new images with generative models, continued
1.text: Create new images with generative models. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create new images with generative models, continued
1.text: Create new images with generative models. client dot images dot generate. The image generation call. model gpt image-one. The deployment name of the image model. prompt. The description of the picture. n one. How many images. size, quality. Dimensions and quality level. result dot data zero dot base sixty-four json. The image as base sixty-four text. Exam tip: To create a picture use images.generate; to understand a picture use a chat call with an image part. Write clear, specific prompts for images too: subject, style, setting, mood. Exam tip: To interpret a picture use a vision-enabled multimodal model; to create a picture use images.generate.

1.title: A vision application with Azure Vision
1.text: A vision application with Azure Vision. Azure Vision image analysis returns structured information about an image: caption, tags, objects with bounding boxes, text (Read), people. Use it when you need consistent, labeled results rather than free-form language, or you do not want to deploy a generative model. Newer designs often prefer a multimodal model for open questions.

1.title: A vision application with Azure Vision, continued
1.text: A vision application with Azure Vision. "Describe this picture in a sentence and answer follow-up questions". Multimodal model. "Return the list of objects and where they are". Azure Vision object detection. "Read the text on a sign". Azure Vision Read (O C R) or a multimodal model. "Create a poster image from a description". Image-generation model.

1.title: Responsible use
1.text: Responsible use. Images can contain people and personal data: follow privacy rules (Module one), tell users when A I-generated images are used (transparency), and check generated images for harmful or biased content.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants customers to upload a photo of a damaged tent and get a written description of the damage. Which kind of model fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A vision-enabled multimodal model. A multimodal model with vision can interpret the image sent in the prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. In a request, how is a question about an image sent to a multimodal chat model? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The user message content is a list with a text part and an image part. The user content is a list that mixes text and an image U R L or base sixty-four data.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A marketing app must create a poster picture from a written description. Which call fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: client.images.generate with an image model. Image generation creates a new image from a text prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. The image-generation call returns base sixty-four json. What does the app need to do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Decode the base sixty-four data to get the image. The image comes back as base sixty-four text that the app decodes and saves or displays.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A solution must return the objects in a photo with their positions in a stable format. Which option fits well? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Vision object detection. Azure Vision object detection returns objects and bounding boxes.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Why must the deployed model be "vision-enabled"? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Otherwise it cannot accept images in the prompt. Text-only models cannot interpret image input.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which kind of model interprets an image in a prompt? Answer: A vision-enabled multimodal model. Question two. What are the two parts of a user message with an image? Answer: A text part and an image part. Question three. Which call creates images? Answer: images.generate.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. In what form does G P T image one return the image? Answer: Base sixty-four data. Question five. Which model was retired on March four, two thousand twenty-six? Answer: dall-e-three. Question six. Which service returns captions, tags and objects? Answer: Azure Vision image analysis.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Interpret: vision-enabled multimodal model; user content list: text part plus image url part (U R L or base sixty-four). Create: images.generate(model, prompt, n, size, quality). Azure Vision: caption, tags, objects, Read, people: structured results. Model names: change quickly; dall-e-three retired March four, two thousand twenty-six. Responsible use: privacy, label A I images, check for harm and bias. In the next module, we continue the course.
